prompt: A sandwich chain's revenue is flat, but its profit fell 20%. Food costs rose from 30% to 38% of revenue. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Ingredient prices have likely risen faster than menu prices.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd check cost per sandwich by ingredient over the last two years.

options.text: It could be ingredient prices, waste, theft, menu mix or supplier contracts.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: Supplier price hikes caused the drop, so the chain should renegotiate its contracts.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: Something has gone wrong on the cost side of the business.
options.feedback: This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: Food cost rising 8 points of revenue explains most of the profit drop. The hypothesis names a likely cause (ingredient prices outpacing menu prices) and the data to test it.

distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be ingredient prices, waste, theft, menu mix or supplier contracts.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: Supplier price hikes caused the drop, so the chain should renegotiate its contracts.
distractor_flaws.M.untestable_hypothesis: Something has gone wrong on the cost side of the business.
